facts.text: Thresholds are the numbers at which a system changes its behavior; filters are rules that prevent the system from reacting to a single noisy measurement.
facts.quote: Thresholds are the numbers at which the system changes its behavior, and filters are the rules that stop it from reacting to a single noisy measurement.

facts.text: Collision systems use a detection confidence threshold to set how sure perception software must be before an object counts.
facts.quote: Detection confidence threshold: how sure the perception software must be before an object counts.

facts.text: Collision systems can use N-of-M frame confirmation, accepting an object only when it appears in a specified number of recent sensor frames; the passage gives 3 of the last 4 frames as an example.
facts.quote: Confirmation, or N-of-M frames: the object must appear in, say, 3 of the last 4 sensor frames before it is accepted.

facts.text: ISO 16001 requires detection to be unambiguous with an uninterrupted sequence of the signal and allows at most 300 ms of detection time.
facts.quote: ISO 16001 asks for detection "unambiguously with an uninterrupted sequence of the signal" and allows at most 300 ms of detection time [Chapter 3].

facts.text: Collision-system persistence and debounce settings determine how long a condition must hold before the system acts and how long before the system stands down.
facts.quote: Persistence and debounce times: how long a condition must hold before the system acts, and how long before it stands down.

facts.text: Collision-system risk determination combines the confirmed object, its position and movement, and the machine's own motion into a collision-risk level.
facts.quote: Risk determination: the step that combines the confirmed object, its position and movement, and the machine's own motion into a collision-risk level.

facts.text: ISO 21815-3 places collision-system intervention at risk level 4 or above.
facts.quote: ISO 21815-3 places intervention at level 4 or above [Chapter 8].

facts.text: Collision-system hysteresis uses different values for switching on and switching off, with the off value safer, to prevent flickering between states.
facts.quote: Hysteresis: the system switches on at one value and off at a different, safer value, so it does not flicker between states.

facts.text: The booklet recommends hysteresis and an explicit brake-release condition after an automatic stop; on slopes, the brake must never be released merely because an object disappears for one sensor frame.
facts.quote: The booklet applies this after an automatic stop: use hysteresis and an explicit release condition, and on slopes never release the brake because the object disappeared for one sensor frame [Chapter 8].

facts.text: Collision-system filters trade speed for reliability: more confirmation frames reduce false alarms but delay braking.
facts.quote: Every filter trades speed for reliability. More confirmation frames mean fewer false alarms but a later brake

facts.text: At 15 km/h and 10 sensor frames per second, each extra confirmation frame costs about 0.4 m of travel before braking.
facts.quote: at 15 km/h and 10 frames per second, each extra frame costs about 0.4 m.

facts.text: The booklet identifies confidence thresholds, zone dimensions per speed, N-of-M filters, persistence and debounce times, time-to-collision triggers, and filter constants as decision variables for collision-system tuning.
facts.quote: The booklet lists them as the decision variables of the tuning problem (confidence thresholds, zone dimensions per speed, N-of-M filters, persistence and debounce times, time-to-collision triggers, filter constants)

facts.text: Collision-system tuning trades off missed or late interventions, false warnings per hour, unnecessary brake events per hour, intervention timing, and time stopped.
facts.quote: the outcomes they trade against each other: missed or late interventions, false warnings per hour, unnecessary brake events per hour, intervention timing and time stopped [Chapter 9].

facts.text: The transition from partial to full braking should depend on the remaining stopping margin and its uncertainty, rather than range alone.
facts.quote: The transition from partial to full braking should depend on the remaining stopping margin and its uncertainty, not on range alone [Chapter 8].
